name: busy-office
description: Busy Office skills for Claude Code: progress-dashboard (one-page stakeholder status), loop-doctor (design of a scheduled autonomous loop), loop-economist (what the loop's actual runs cost and produced) requeue (reprioritise and sharpen the queue the loop is fed) sharpen-intent (make the purpose document steer) loop-atlas (the loop as one picture, the crew as a card deck) wake-weight (what every run pays before it starts) solo-flow (trunk-based git workflow for a repo with exactly one writer) graph-engineer (redraw a linear agent as an orchestration graph, review and lint Workflow scripts, estimate the bill) jev (a typed second opinion from jev-ai.pro — PASS / REVIEW / FAIL before claiming done, routing, trusting research, releasing or a risky tool call; the API key is asked for at install). Shape-detecting, read-only collectors with fixtures and a cross-collector drift check; reports graded by a blind critic against a written bar, with a mechanical pre-check that settles word budgets, headline figures against a fresh collection, and every citation.

api_key.title: jev-ai.pro API key
api_key.description: For the jev skill. Create one at jev-ai.pro → API Keys. Leave empty to skip; set it later with /plugin configure busy-office.

add_to_path.title: Add jev to your Terminal
add_to_path.description: For the jev skill: link ~/.local/bin/jev to this plugin so plain `jev` works in a Terminal, kept pointing at the current version after updates. Never replaces a file it didn't make.

allow_all_repos.title: Allow all repos to send to Jev
allow_all_repos.description: For the jev skill: let every repo on this machine send to jev-ai.pro, except repos you block with `jev deny` — the same as `jev allow --all`. Off: allow repos one by one with `jev allow` in a Terminal.
